changes.before:
Facebook and Instagram advertising can help a service business show its work, explain an offer and invite people to make contact. To decide whether it deserves investment, connect those possibilities to a service you can deliver, evidence you can show and enquiries your team can assess and handle.

The first question is what the campaign should achieve. The next is how you will recognise a useful result. A low cost per click or form submission can be encouraging, but it does not establish that suitable work is entering the business.

This guide covers the decisions to make before investing: objective, offer, audience, creative material, contact route, budget, measurement and follow-up. It focuses on Australian service businesses rather than a sequence of buttons in an advertising interface.
changes.after:
Before you spend on Facebook and Instagram ads, be clear about the work you want to attract and what happens when someone responds. The campaign can show your service and prompt contact. Your team still needs to assess whether each request fits.

Say you run a residential landscaping business serving selected Perth suburbs. You design and build gardens, but you do not offer routine maintenance. This is a hypothetical example. An ad that simply promises “all your garden needs” leaves people guessing and can bring requests you cannot take on.

Start with an offer you can explain and support, then plan the creative, contact route and follow-up around it. A low cost per click or form submission is only part of the picture. You need to know what arrived, whether it suited your business and what it cost to handle.

changes.after: For the Perth landscaper, that means showing garden design and construction, making the service area clear and explaining what a quote request involves. If routine maintenance is not available, the ad and destination should make that clear too.
